messages:
lincoln-ops: Hey crew, hitting an issue where ~8-12% of checkout requests show up in our logs but the Console trace view says "No trace found for request_id". Seen across two customers (acme & beta-shop).
lincoln-ops: Example request IDs: rq_chk_9f4b2a, rq_chk_c7d1ee. Happened around 2024-06-18T14:02:10Z -> 14:10:00Z. Logs show span upload succeeded (200) but trace panel can't link.
support-bot: Thanks for the report, @lincoln-ops — filing internal ticket and pinging eng-sre. Reference: INC-2024-172.
mia: @lincoln-ops can you paste one full request_id and the exact timestamp of the log entry? also which region/cluster (us-west-2?)
lincoln-ops: rq_chk_9f4b2a @ 2024-06-18T14:04:22Z. Cluster: us-west-2a. Log line: "spans/ingest 200 ok request_id=rq_chk_9f4b2a size=3k"
jordan: quick question — are these short traces (1-3 spans) or larger? small traces sometimes fall into a different pipeline.
lincoln-ops: small, mostly 2 spans (frontend->checkout service).
omar: I pulled logs for that time window. I see a few 5xx from the span-indexer around 14:03:50Z that correlate with a retry path. Possible the indexer returned 502 for a subset and client retried without idempotency, causing partial ingestion. Snippet: ```2024-06-18T14:03:50Z ERROR span-indexer batch=42 status=502 shard=5 trace_id=...```
mia: can you run a console query to look up by request_id? in the Console -> Traces search box try `request_id:rq_chk_9f4b2a OR log.request_id:rq_chk_9f4b2a` and share results.
jordan: also run this backend check (internal tooling): ```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://internal-api.redwood/trace/lookup?request_id=rq_chk_9f4b2a" | jq .```
lincoln-ops: ran both — Console search returns no linked trace but logs endpoint shows the log event, and the `internal-api/trace/lookup` returns HTTP 404 (no canonical trace), despite spans being in raw store S3 with key `spans/us-west-2/2024-06-18/14/9f/9f4b2a.json`.
omar: that suggests indexing step failed or index entry dropped. Two possibilities: (1) span-indexer returned error and client didn't retry index step, (2) index write succeeded but the search index got inconsistent due to a compaction bug we saw last month.
eng-sre: Adding repro steps to collect consistent artifacts:
- From customer: capture the raw span object (S3 path) and the ingest response headers.
- From infra: check span-indexer logs for 14:00-14:15Z and grep for `request_id=rq_chk_9f4b2a`.
- From search: run `es-get doc id=span-idx-<computed-id>` to confirm doc exists.
eng-sre: Quick repro curl to push a minimal synthetic trace: ```curl -X POST https://ingest.redwood/v1/spans -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"request_id":"rq_chk_test123","spans":[{"id":"s1","parent_id":null,"name":"frontend"},{"id":"s2","parent_id":"s1","name":"checkout"}]}' -v```
mia: good — if folks can run that and then check Console -> Traces for `rq_chk_test123` we can confirm end-to-end. If you can reproduce, capture the ingest response (200 vs 502) and the timestamp.
lincoln-ops: ran synthetic. Ingest returned 200 and raw span object landed in S3, but Console still shows "No trace found". I can share S3 key.
omar: ok that proves indexing is the gap. I'm seeing a retry/backoff mis-handle in the span-indexer client around cases where batch size > 512KB; retries were treated as partial success and didn't requeue index writes. Pushing a tentative fix to handle partial-failures correctly.
jordan: action items:
- Omar to open PR with fix and unit test for partial-index failures.
- Eng-sre to kick a reindex job for the affected window (2024-06-18T13:55Z -> 2024-06-18T14:15Z).
- Support to notify customers and provide workaround (search raw logs with `log.request_id:...`) until index repaired.
mia: approximate ETA for reindex job?
eng-sre: reindex job scheduled (low priority) will start in ~2h, estimate 3-4h run time for that window. If PR merges and deploys can accelerate. I'll post ticket updates in #incidents.
lincoln-ops: thanks. Please confirm when reindex completes — those customers are reporting checkout friction.
support-bot: INC-2024-172 updated: status=investigating assigned=eng-sre severity=high :eyes:
omar: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/span-indexer/pulls/342 fix: handle partial batch failures. CI green locally, will request review.
jordan: temporary mitigation: turning on the Console setting "Allow fallback trace linking from raw logs" will show a best-effort link. Not ideal but reduces customer impact.
lincoln-ops: tried fallback, shows logs link — acceptable for now. Any chance of data loss for those spans?
omar: no data loss — spans are in raw store. It's an index consistency problem; reindex will rebuild search docs.
mia: thanks everyone. I'll keep the customers updated and will paste reindex job link when started. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
eng-sre: will follow up with postmortem once root cause confirmed and patch deployed.
lincoln-ops: appreciated.
summary: Customer reported unlinked checkout request IDs; root cause: span-indexer partial failure/failed indexing leading to traces not linked in Console; actions: PR, reindex job, customer workaround provided
